statements.t: While we treat patients of all ages, most of our patients are 65 and older, and the number of Medicare enrollees is expected to continue to grow for the foreseeable future.
More specifically, the average age of our Medicare patients is approximately 77, and the population group for ages 75 and older is expected to grow at approximately 4% per year through 2030.
We believe the demand for the services we provide will continue to increase as the U.S. population ages.

Based on our analysis that utilizes the acuity of our patients annualized over a twelve-month period ended June 30, 2026, our experience with outlier payments over this same time frame, and other factors, we believe the 2027 Final IRF Rule will result in a net increase to our Medicare payment rates of approximately 2.3% effective October 1, 2026.
With this expansion, 108 of our IRFs (representing approximately 63% of our IRF Medicare claims) will be subject to RCD.
We have engaged, and will continue to engage, with the MAC and CMS to ensure the review process is consistent with existing rules, regulations and statutes.
In the case of new-store volume growth, the addition of hospitals to our portfolio also may be difficult and take longer than expected.
We remain confident in the prospects of our business based on the increasing demands for the services we provide to an aging population.
We expect Depreciation and amortization to increase going forward as a result of our recent and ongoing capital investments.
In certain jurisdictions, we do not expect to generate sufficient income to use all available state net operating losses and foreign tax credits prior to their expiration.

This determination is based on our evaluation of all available evidence in these jurisdictions including results of operations during the preceding three years, our forecast of future earnings, and prudent tax planning strategies.

It is possible we may be required to increase or decrease our valuation allowance at some future time if our forecast of future earnings varies from actual results on a consolidated basis or in the applicable tax jurisdiction, if the timing of future tax deductions differs from our expectations, or pursuant to changes in state and foreign tax laws and rates.

Our capital expenditures include costs associated with our hospital renovation program, de novo projects, capacity expansions, technology initiatives, and building and equipment upgrades and purchases.
During 2026, we expect to spend approximately $920 million to $995 million for capital expenditures using cash on hand and borrowings under our revolving credit facility.
At September 30, 2026, we have projects under construction which have an estimated additional cost to complete over the next two years of approximately $535 million.
We expect to fund capital expenditures using cash on hand and borrowings under our revolving credit facility.
We expect quarterly dividends to be paid in January, April, July, and October.

However, the actual declaration of any future cash dividends, and the setting of record and payment dates as well as the per share amounts, will be at the discretion of our board of directors after consideration of various factors, including our capital position and alternative uses of funds.
Cash dividends are expected to be funded using cash flows from operations, cash on hand, and availability under our revolving credit facility.
Future repurchases under this authorization generally are expected to be funded using a combination of cash on hand and availability under our $1 billion revolving credit facility.

If we anticipated a potential covenant violation, we would seek relief from our lenders, which would have some cost to us, and such relief might be on terms less favorable to us than those in our existing credit agreement.
The plan also provides that dividends paid on the shares held for the accounts of the directors will be reinvested in shares of our common stock which will also be held in the trust.

Excluding net operating revenues, the Company does not provide guidance on a GAAP basis because it is unable to predict, with reasonable certainty, the future impact of items that are deemed to be outside the control of the Company or otherwise not indicative of its ongoing operating performance.
